newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Newcrest denies Normandy margin call rumour.
newsitem.headline: Newcrest denies Normandy margin call rumour.

text.p: Newcrest Mining Ltd rejected market rumours on Thursday that it faced a margin call from ANZ Securities on its February equity-gold swap arrangement over its 11.9 percent stake in Normandy Mining Ltd.
Newcrest investor relations manager David Sasson told Reuters that Newcrest was well short of the trigger point which would force Newcrest to lodge a margin with ANZ.

Brokers and analysts have said a rumour that Newcrest faced a margin call of over A$30 million on the deal had thumped Newcrest's shares down by as much as 28 cents or over 11 percent to as low as A$2.20 in panicked Thursday morning trade.
Newcrest swapped its 192.7 million Normandy shares for 740,000 ounces of gold under the two-year equity-for-gold swap in February.

But under the agreement Newcrest must make a deposit with ANZ if the difference between the value of the Normandy stake and the Australian dollar value of the gold is greater than A$66 million for more than 10 consecutive days, Sasson said.
That deposit is repaid once the differential falls below A$66 million for more than 10 consecutive days.
Currently, the Normandy stake is worth A$262.1 million, given Normandy's unchanged share price of A$1.36, while the gold is valued at A$317.5 million, given gold is valued at A$429 an ounce.
This gives a difference of A$55.4 million, well below the A$66 million trigger.

"If the differential value between Normandy and the Australian dollar gold price exceeds A$66 million for more than 10 consecutive days, we have to pay the difference between A$66 and whatever that number is," Sasson said.
"If it goes to A$70 million for more than 10 days we have to lodge with the ANZ Bank A$4 million on deposit in a special account where we get paid interest on the A$4 million," he said.
This might involve a simple transfer of other Newcrest money deposited with ANZ from one account to another, he said.
"When it falls below A$66 million for more than 10 days, that money that was lodged gets transferred back out to whereever we nominate," Sasson said.
The gap was currently somewhere between A$50 million and A$55 million, he said.
Newcrest's shares had bounced back to A$2.31 by 12.50 p.m. (0250 GMT), down 17 cents on Wednesday's close.
